title: Cubit
tagline: A modern speedcubing platform that blends timing, training, coaching, and community into one seamless experience.
shortDescription: An open-source web platform for cubers that unifies precision timing, session tracking, statistics, interactive training modules, gamification, and community features into one seamless experience.
description: Cubit is an open-source web platform built specifically for cubers. It brings solving, training, learning, progress tracking, competition, and community into one focused experience. Currently in Pre-Launch — V1 Final QA.

caseStudy.problem: Cubers often have to juggle disparate tools for timing, scramble generation, algorithm learning, progress tracking, and community interaction without a unified, modern interface.
caseStudy.solution: Built a comprehensive full-stack speedcubing platform combining a precision hold-to-start timer, custom cube visualization engine, 8-module/51-lesson interactive Trainer, append-only rating ledger, and real-time community capabilities.
features: Precision speedcubing timer with hold-to-start & +2/DNF penalties
Solve logging, personal bests, Ao5/Ao12 & statistics trends
Custom cube-state engine, algorithm playback & 2D net visualization
Cubit Trainer: 8 learning modules & 51 canonical interactive lessons
Gamification: append-only rating ledger, streaks & milestone rewards
Real-time community feed, friendships, leaderboards & notifications
Focus Mode with dedicated solving environment & original audio
caseStudy.challenges: Designing an accurate cube-state visualization engine for 2x2 through 5x5 cubes, ensuring sub-millisecond timer responsiveness, and establishing an append-only rating reconciliation pipeline.
caseStudy.outcome: Core V1 development is complete with extensive documentation (PRD, HLD, LLD, API Blueprint). The platform is currently undergoing final full-product QA before its initial public V1 release.
caseStudy.learnings: Architecting modular state systems with Zustand, managing complex matrix transformations for Rubik's cubes, and designing scalable real-time architectures with Socket.IO and Prisma.
